title.narrative: Restoration and connectivity of priority habitats for species conservation in Serbia (KBF)

description.narrative: The project aims to restore degraded old-growth forests, wetlands, and grasslands while enhancing ecological connectivity through innovative, participatory approaches. Vulnerable pilot sites will be assessed to guide tailored restoration measures such as reforestation and wetlands rewetting, implemented via a competitive Challenge Call involving stakeholders to promote employment, skills development, and women’s leadership. Legal, regulatory, and financial frameworks will be updated to align with EU directives and international commitments, integrating climate resilience, biodiversity standards, and private sector support, including women-led enterprises. Public awareness and stakeholder knowledge will be strengthened through workshops, campaigns, and educational programs, prioritizing gender equity and community engagement. Robust risk management, monitoring, and evaluation systems will ensure sustained results, aligning with biodiversity targets and international standards

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
